# OA.5 Numerical checks {#num}

Section 4 of the paper computes date-specific Markov policy functions by backward induction along the demographic
transition, and selects among the candidate equilibria at each state; the technical documentation
[@BergGE26doc] gives the algorithms and the code. This chapter reports two checks of that computation.

## OA.5.1 Date-specific and stationary policies {#num-stationary}

The table prints the gap between the date-specific solution and a time-invariant policy function, the
approximation of much of the quantitative politico-economic literature, at the same dates. Section 4 summarizes it in a footnote.

{{< include _generated/groups/num-stationary.qmd >}}

## OA.5.2 Equilibrium selection {#num-selection}

The table prints, for every file of results behind an exhibit, the largest number of equilibria and of candidate
solutions found at any state, and the number of states at which no candidate passed the equilibrium test and the
solver fell back on the integral rule of the technical documentation. A single equilibrium at every state means
that the selection rule of section 4 never had to choose. A file prints no count where its solve selects no tax,
the economic-equilibrium paths, or where its driver did not record the count: the calibration grids of the U.S.,
the UK and France, the Frisch-elasticity and timing files, and the tax layer of the CRRA endogenous-design
calibration and path files, whose design layer is counted in the lower panel. The paper's statement in section 4
rests on the files that record the count.
